Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — deployment mode (shared vs dedicated)

Thanks again for the call today, Kenji — great context on FinPay's payment API workload. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary of needs
- Target production traffic: ~1.2k QPS peak, average ~300 QPS off-peak
- Latency targets: p95 ~200ms for short-generation calls (single-turn prompts), p99 < 350ms for complex flows
- Regulated workloads in scope for a subset of customers in the EU (data residency)
- Primary concern: noisy-neighbor impact on latency and tail spikes if using shared hosted pool

What we discussed
- Hosted API (shared): fastest onboarding, but less isolation guarantees; mitigations like priority routing and prefix caching can help
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool for isolation and predictable throughput; supports stricter SLOs and isolation boundaries
- Private VPC/on-prem: considered for very sensitive accounts — higher setup time and cost

Next steps (action items)
1) I'll share a sizing and SLO matrix for both Hosted + mitigation patterns and Dedicated capacity (attached: redwood-dedicated-sizing.pdf, slo-matrix.xlsx).
2) Priyom to provide benchmark notes on noisy-neighbor isolation and autoscaling behavior.
3) Let's schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review benchmarks and a pilot plan (canary + failover).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.pdf (pdf, 3 pages), slo-matrix.xlsx (excel, 2 sheets)

Thanks,

Hi Kenji — joining in with technical details based on our perf/ops playbook. TL;DR: hosted mitigations help, but Dedicated gives predictable tail behavior. Notes below: 

Hosted (shared) mitigations- Traffic policing: token-based priority queues and rate limiting reduce chance of single-tenant spikes affecting others.
- Prefix/KV caching: reduces upstream compute for repeated patterns (useful for prompt templates).
- Smart routing + graceful degradation: route to cheaper model variants or reduced max_tokens when SLOs are at risk.
- Fallback time: with our routing, failover to a reserved burst pool typically initiates within 10s-30s, but warm-up can add latency during initial warm-up.

Dedicated capacity (recommended for strict SLOs)- Reserved GPU pool with tenant isolation (no shared kernels on the same host), deterministic queueing and pre-warmed kernels.
- Tail latencies: consistent p95/p99 observed in our benchmarks (see slo-matrix.xlsx) because of fixed capacity and isolation.
- Autoscaling/overprovision: can configure burst capacity and autoscale thresholds to protect p95 during short spikes.

Operational notes- Canary plan: run a 2-week Dedicated trial for a subset of traffic (10-20%) and monitor SLOs/p99 under real traffic.
- Metrics to capture: request QPS distribution, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, request queue depth.
- Incident references: we anonymize and can share redacted posts about noisy-neighbor incidents; most resolved by routing + reserved burst pools.

I attached a short benchmarking summary and SLO matrix (redwood-dedicated-sizing.pdf, slo-matrix.xlsx). Happy to walk through numbers on a call — available Tue/Wed next week.

Cheers,
